title: Maintaining Correct Drain Pipe Slope
description: Proper slope in horizontal drainage piping is critical for maintaining self-scouring velocity. If a pipe is flat or back-pitched, wastewater stalls, allowing solid debris and grease to settle and form stubborn blockages over time. Conversely, excessive slope can cause liquids to flow faster than solid waste, leaving dry debris behind inside the line. Standard residential drainage typically targets a consistent slope, often 1/4 inch per foot for smaller pipes, subject to local plumbing codes. Periodic inspection of pipe hangers and supports prevents sagging and belly formation along horizontal drain runs.

Standard residential drainage typically targets a consistent slope, often 1/4 inch per foot for smaller pipes, subject to local plumbing codes. Periodic inspection of pipe hangers and supports prevents sagging and belly formation along horizontal drain runs.
